notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/festo-se__festo-dev-applied-motion --backend fake (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed: the R2 hardware backend is refused until reviewed_by is set; the hardware factory and the applied_motion package were never imported or run, and no hardware test was performed. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card names PythonObjectDriver, but the package is a direct decorated Driver over the card entry symbol applied_motion.backends.fposbapi_client:FPosBAPIClient. The motion action combines MOVE_LOC with a ROB_POS read-back and a cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 output, which the family's static result map cannot express. All card entry symbols were confirmed in the clone; FPosBAPIClient is used rather than Gantry because Gantry has no halt/stop method (the FPosBAPI stop path is FPosBAPIClient.halt) and FPosBAPIClient has the parameter and diagnostics methods. COVERAGE: reads position (ROB_POS), global_speed (parameter 103), sys_status, error_active, error_text and fieldbus_error; write global_speed (operator_required, filled by site-limits.example.json); actions x-cap.festo-se.home_axes.v1 (HOME), cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 (MOVE_LOC) and x-cap.festo-se.halt_motion.v1 (HALT, safe_state=True); @estop, @reset (RESET_ERR) and teardown (socket close). device_kind is robot.arm because cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 binds only robot.arm; the machine is a 3-axis Cartesian gantry. risk is R2, above the card floor R1, because the library commands real mechanical motion. The x/y/z workspace and the global speed are Limit.operator_required: the clone states the units but not the travel or speed envelope of a configured machine. The home and halt operations are extensions because the catalogue classes publish optional inputs the native HOME/HALT cannot honor. NOT COVERED: the Modbus/festo-edcon backend (EdconAxis), per-axis MOVE_AXIS velocity control, move_pos/move_path/teach/read_pos/write_pos/tray/VEAB/open_valve, and the Gantry wrapper; only the FPosBAPI TCP client is exercised. The current position is parsed from the client's documented ROB_POS response layout because FPosBAPIClient has no current-position getter. The e-stop and the safe-state action both send HALT on the same serialized socket as a running motion command, so stop latency depends on the PLC answering the outstanding command first; the clone documents no independent hardware e-stop, so estop_physical_ref is not claimed and safety.not_certified is true. No gate warnings: check-report.json has empty findings in G1-G9. check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package; the digest above is the one the passing run printed.
